title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
abstract: arXiv:2611.18434v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA into four Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) severity groups. tldr: 该论文扩展了SleepXAI睡眠分期框架，系统比较五种XAI方法，并以AASM定义的脑电频段的Spearman秩相关评估归因保真度，实现了基于单通道脑电、兼顾分类性能与临床可解释性的睡眠阶段分类。
en_tdlr: This paper extends the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five XAI methods, evaluating attribution fidelity via Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, enabling explainable sleep stage classification using single-channel EEG.
